verdicts.what_they_do: Logistics: they move around 40,000 shipments a day across North America.
verdicts.why: Three open infrastructure roles this quarter and they say outright they are standing up a platform team from scratch, on their own EKS at about 140 engineers. Cloud spend outgrowing volume for six quarters with an executive asking monthly is the cost conversation we win.
verdicts.hook: You have three infrastructure roles open and an exec asking monthly which service is driving the EKS bill. That attribution question is usually a tooling problem before it is a headcount problem.

verdicts.what_they_do: Scheduling and intake software for outpatient clinics, in a HIPAA environment.
verdicts.why: Two infrastructure openings in one month, and the posting states plainly that they are eighteen months into a Kubernetes migration where the observability story has not kept up. About 90 engineers, which is inside the range.
verdicts.hook: Eighteen months into a migration where observability has not kept up is the exact point where teams discover their HIPAA constraints rule out half the market.

verdicts.what_they_do: A staffing firm that places senior infrastructure engineers.
verdicts.why: The skip rules name staffing agencies and recruiters directly: both postings are on behalf of an undisclosed client, so the buying signal belongs to a company we cannot see from here. Nothing to work until the client is named.

verdicts.what_they_do: Series C payments infrastructure, around 200 engineers.
verdicts.why: The posting says the first thing the hire owns is migrating off self-hosted Prometheus, which has become a second full-time job for two people. That is an active, funded, already-admitted problem, and 200 engineers on latency SLOs sits at the top of our range.
verdicts.hook: Two people spending half their time keeping self-hosted Prometheus alive is a cost you can put a number on before you ever price a replacement.

verdicts.what_they_do: A high-cardinality metrics and tracing platform ingesting 4 trillion data points a day.
verdicts.why: Their whole product is observability, which the skip rules rule out as a competitor rather than a buyer. Strong infrastructure signal, wrong side of the table.

verdicts.what_they_do: Collaborative tools for illustrators, twelve people total.
verdicts.why: One founding full-stack role at a company with five engineers and no other infra hiring, which the signal rules call out as the absence of a platform team rather than a signal. They are on Render and say they intend to stay there.

The title is an infrastructure role, which is the signal, but the posting is entirely benefits copy: no engineering headcount, no stack, nothing about what they run. Worth thirty seconds on their site before anyone spends a week on it.
